statements.t: “Our headstart in speed to power is a key reason an investment-grade hyperscaler has signed up for 600 megawatts and committed more than $200 million up front to accelerate construction at Project Matador with an additional $90 million contemplated.

These agreements demonstrate Fermi’s strategy of investing early in infrastructure readiness to enable faster customer development, attract customer capital earlier in the project lifecycle, and translate our power and infrastructure advantages into long-term revenue opportunities with little or no dilution.

Earlier this week, Texas Tech University System Chancellor, Brandon Creighton, issued a statement reaffirming the partnership: “Texas Tech is proud of our partnership with Fermi and remains firmly committed to the success of Project Matador.”
